key_sub: Resistors in series add; in parallel the total resistance is smaller.
body_html:
How to think about it

The emf of a battery is the potential difference across it when no current flows. Current I is the rate of flow of charge: Q = IΔt. An ammeter is connected in series; a voltmeter is connected in parallel across a component.

In series the current is the same everywhere and the potential differences add up to the emf; R = R₁ + R₂. In parallel the potential difference is the same across each branch and the currents add; 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.

Example

2 A flows for 30 s. Charge?

Q = IΔt

Answer: 60 C

Example

4 Ω and 4 Ω in parallel. Total resistance?

1/R = 1/4 + 1/4

Answer: 2 Ω

Common mistakes

  • Connecting a voltmeter in series.
  • Thinking current is used up in a circuit.
  • Adding parallel resistances like series ones.

faq.q: Why are houses wired in parallel?
faq.a: Each appliance gets the full potential difference and can be switched on and off on its own.

faq.q: What happens to the total resistance when you add a resistor in parallel?
faq.a: It decreases, because there is another path for the current.
